title: Max out your HSA
whoFor: Anyone with a high-deductible health plan, employed or self-employed
description: Every dollar you put in lowers your taxable income, grows tax-free, and comes out tax-free for medical costs — the only "triple tax-free" account there is.
impact: Up to ~$1,000–$2,000/year for a household maxing out $4,300–$8,550

title: Check the new 2025 tips or overtime deduction
whoFor: Tipped workers (servers, bartenders, drivers, salon staff) and hourly employees earning overtime
description: Brand-new for 2025 — lets you deduct up to $25,000 of tips and/or up to $12,500–$25,000 of overtime pay, on top of everything else.
impact: Could be worth $1,000–$6,000+ depending on your tip/overtime income

title: Bunch your charitable giving
whoFor: Anyone who donates to charity and is close to (but under) the standard deduction
description: Give two years' worth every other year — often through a Donor-Advised Fund — so you clear the standard-deduction threshold and actually get a tax benefit from giving.
impact: Can turn $0 of tax benefit into $1,000–$3,000+ in a bunched year

title: Harvest investment losses before December 31
whoFor: Any investor with stocks, funds, or crypto that have lost value
description: Selling a losing investment on purpose lets you offset gains elsewhere — and up to $3,000 of regular income — free money you're otherwise leaving on the table.
impact: Worth 22–37 cents in tax savings per dollar of loss you realize

title: Confirm every dependent's Social Security number is on file
whoFor: Parents and guardians of children under 17
description: A missing or late SSN forfeits the entire Child Tax Credit — a paperwork fix, not a strategy, but a full $2,200 per child if missed.

title: Check the Earned Income Credit, even if you assume you don't qualify
whoFor: Part-time workers, gig workers, and the self-employed with modest income
description: One of the most overlooked credits among non-traditional earners — many assume gig/freelance income doesn't count, but it does.
impact: Up to $649 with no children, $4,328 with one, $7,152 with two, $8,046 with three or more

title: Use a Qualified Charitable Distribution if you're 70½ or older
whoFor: Retirees with a traditional IRA who also give to charity
description: Send money straight from your IRA to charity instead of taking a taxable withdrawal — it satisfies your required withdrawal without adding a dollar of taxable income.
impact: Can shelter thousands of dollars of otherwise-taxable IRA withdrawals per year

title: Consider an S-corp election once profit is substantial
whoFor: Freelancers and small-business owners with consistent, healthy profit
description: Splitting income into a reasonable salary plus distributions can reduce the extra 15.3% self-employment tax on part of your profit — though it adds payroll/compliance costs.
impact: Can save several thousand dollars a year once profit is high enough

title: Track mileage and home-office expenses from day one
whoFor: Gig/delivery drivers, freelancers, and anyone working from home
description: Usually the single biggest deduction for these groups, and the easiest one to under-claim if you don't track it from the start.
impact: Often $2,000–$5,000+ a year for active drivers or home-based freelancers

title: Ask about a state pass-through entity tax election
whoFor: Business owners with an S-corp or partnership in a state that allows it
description: A state-level election lets your business deduct state tax at the entity level, sidestepping the $40,000 individual cap on state and local tax deductions.
impact: Can be worth thousands for business owners in higher-tax states above the cap
